fixes.explanation: I get it, friend. When I hear "fire," I want the oven timer reset too. But Jesus says the opposite: "…how I wish it were already kindled!" (Luke 12:49). He isn't asking for more time. He wants it burning already.

Not this one, friend. Jesus says He came to ignite this fire, and then adds, "…how I wish it were already kindled!" (Luke 12:49). That's a wish for it to be burning, not for it to go out. Nothing in His words says He wants it put out.

You got it, baker. Jesus doesn't ease into this one. He asks, "Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth?" and then answers Himself: "No, I tell you, but division." (Luke 12:51). I think He asks it as a question because He knows what the crowd is expecting. Then He tells them plainly what He means.

Healing is a good word, friend. But in this verse Jesus says, "Do you think that I have come to bring peace to the earth? No, I tell you, but division." (Luke 12:51). Division is the word He picks here. Healing doesn't show up.

Wind is close, friend, since it shows up in the very next verse. There Jesus says that when the south wind blows, you say, "It will be hot," (Luke 12:55). But for the cloud rising in the west, the crowds say, "A shower is coming…" (Luke 12:54). That one's rain.

Right, friend. Jesus asks, "And why don’t you judge for yourselves what is right?" (Luke 12:57). He's pointing them to judge for themselves, not to let someone else decide. It's like me asking why you'd ask a neighbor if the dough looks right when the bowl is sitting in front of you.

That's the word, baker. Jesus says, "Make every effort to reconcile with your adversary while you are on your way to the magistrate." (Luke 12:58). He doesn't say to wait until the judge is involved. He says to do it on the way, while the road is still open.
